## About:

Code for figure in the manuscript, 'Using State Space Models to improve three-dimensional estimates of great black-backed gull movement in relation to offshore wind development in the Northeast United States' by Nosazeogie et al., under review by Plos ONE

High resolution three-dimensional movement data is provided to demonstrate use of custom three-dimensional state space model code written by Ian Jonsen


Figure 3: Example random-walk state space model estimates of flight altitude from high-resolution tracks of great black-backed gulls relative to raw data (black points). Pink shaded areas show 95% confidence intervals of the SSM. Pink shaded area shows the 95% confidence envelope around the SSM-estimated altitudes (red line).


Data available in dryad: 


PART 1: SSM for high res data (1-120s/1s-2min)

1 sec timestep

(OFFSHORE)

minimum track duration: 120min (2hrs)
maximum gap in track: 4 mins


```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(TMB)
require(tidyverse)
require(sf)
library (here)


data <- read.csv(here("data","Nosazeogie__L1_highresolution_GBBG_for_dryad_oneID.csv"))

# data <- read.csv(here("data", "L1_Jul25_1-120 sec (high res)_min120min_offshore.csv"))

source("fn/ssm_filter.R")
source("fn/ssm_filter_crw.R")


```





Setting up data for SSM

```{r}
d=data

names(d) <- tolower(names(d))
d <- d |>
  ungroup() |>  # Remove any grouping
  mutate(lc = "G") |>
  dplyr::select(id=trip_id, ## SSM is run on each sub-track
                date=utc_datetime,
                lc,
                lon=longitude,
                lat=latitude,
                z=altitude_m,
                hdop) |>
  filter(lon<0, lat>0) |>
  mutate(id = as.character(id))


## reprojection

prj <- "+proj=merc +units=km +datum=WGS84"

d <- d |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(crs = prj)

dxy <- d |> 
  st_coordinates() |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rename(x = X, y = Y)

d <- bind_cols(d, dxy) |>
  dplyr::select(id, date, x, y, z, hdop)
d$geometry <- NULL


```



SSM loop

```{r}
###fitting multiple tracks

##to avoid conflicts with the fuction "select"
select <- dplyr::select

data$device_id=as.character(data$device_id)
str(d$date)
d$date <- as.POSIXct(d$date, format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz="UTC")

library(data.table)

###loop 1 (rw)

### updated resumable loop to rerun the trip_id that was in progress when the session aborted
# checks for data loss from previous aborts

library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# STEP 0: Create output folder if it doesn't exist
ssm_outputs1 <- here("data", "ssm_outputs1")
dir.create(ssm_outputs1, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# STEP 1: Generate unique_combinations
unique_combinations <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(device_id, trip_id) %>%
  distinct()

# STEP 2: Read saved files
cat("✅ SCRIPT STARTED AND RUNNING FROM THE TOP\n")
saved_files <- list.files(ssm_outputs1, pattern = "^ssm_\\d+\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)

cat("🔍 Found saved files:\n")
print(saved_files)

# Extract trip IDs from filenames
saved_trip_ids <- gsub(".*ssm_(\\d+)\\.csv", "\\1", saved_files)
cat("📌 Extracted saved trip_ids:\n")
print(saved_trip_ids)

# STEP 3: Identify most recent trip (in case it crashed before saving)
if (length(saved_trip_ids) > 0) {
  last_saved_file <- saved_files[which.max(file.info(saved_files)$mtime)]
  last_saved_trip_id <- gsub(".*ssm_(\\d+)\\.csv", "\\1", last_saved_file)
  message("✅ DEBUG: This block is running. Last file: ", last_saved_file)
  message("Reprocessing last trip_id in case of crash: ", last_saved_trip_id)
  
  # Remove last one to reprocess it
  saved_trip_ids <- setdiff(saved_trip_ids, last_saved_trip_id)
} else {
  last_saved_trip_id <- NULL
  message("⚠️ No previously saved trip_ids found. Nothing to resume.")
}

# STEP 4: Create filtered list of trips to process
saved_trip_ids <- as.character(saved_trip_ids)
last_saved_trip_id <- if (!is.null(last_saved_trip_id)) as.character(last_saved_trip_id) else NULL
unique_combinations$trip_id <- as.character(unique_combinations$trip_id)

if (is.null(last_saved_trip_id)) {
  trip_ids_to_process <- unique_combinations
} else {
  trip_ids_to_process <- unique_combinations %>%
    filter(!(trip_id %in% saved_trip_ids) | trip_id == last_saved_trip_id)
}

# Diagnostic print
cat("✅ Total unique trips:", nrow(unique_combinations), "\n")
cat("📋 Trips to process (including possible crash trip):", nrow(trip_ids_to_process), "\n")
cat("🧪 First few trip_ids to process:\n")
print(head(trip_ids_to_process$trip_id))


# STEP 5: Loop through each trip and fit the model
for (i in 1:nrow(trip_ids_to_process)) {
  target_device_id <- trip_ids_to_process$device_id[i]
  target_trip_id <- trip_ids_to_process$trip_id[i]
  out_file <- file.path(
    ssm_outputs1,
    paste0("ssm_", target_trip_id, ".csv")
  )
  
  # Fallback safety: skip if file already exists
  if (file.exists(out_file)) {
    message("Skipping ", target_trip_id, " — already processed.")
    next
  }
  
  message(paste("🚀 Processing", i, "of", nrow(trip_ids_to_process), 
                "- Device:", target_device_id, "Trip:", target_trip_id))
  
  subset_data <- subset(d, id == target_trip_id)
  
  if (nrow(subset_data) == 0 || any(is.na(subset_data$date))) {
    message(paste("⛔ Skipping trip", target_trip_id, "— missing or empty data"))
    next
  }
  
  fit1 <- tryCatch({
    ssm_filter(subset_data, time.step = 0.0167/60, df = 4)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message(paste("⚠️ fit1 failed for", target_trip_id, ":", e$message))
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  fit2 <- tryCatch({
    ssm_filter_crw(subset_data, time.step = 0.0167/60, df = 4)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message(paste("⚠️ fit2 failed for", target_trip_id, ":", e$message))
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  if (is.null(fit1) || is.null(fit2)) {
    message(paste("⛔ Skipping trip", target_trip_id, "— one or both models failed"))
    next
  }
  
  predicted_values <- fit1$predicted %>%
    dplyr::select(date, x, y, id) %>%
    left_join(fit1$predicted %>% dplyr::select(date, z, z.se) %>%
                rename(z_fit1 = z, z_fit1.se = z.se), by = "date") %>%
    left_join(fit2$predicted %>% dplyr::select(date, z, z.se) %>%
                rename(z_fit2 = z, z_fit2.se = z.se), by = "date") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(device_id = target_device_id, trip_id = target_trip_id)
  
  write.csv(predicted_values, file = out_file, row.names = FALSE)
  
  # Log progress
  cat(Sys.time(), "- ✅ Saved trip:", target_trip_id, "\n", file = "ssm_outputs1processing_log.txt", append = TRUE)
  
  gc()
}

#### merging
csv_files <- list.files(ssm_outputs1, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)

ssm_df <- bind_rows(lapply(csv_files, function(file) {
  read.csv(

      id = "character",
      device_id = "character",
      trip_id = "character"
    )
  )
}))



```



Plot with SSM output joined to raw data

```{r}
d6 <- read.csv(here("data", "Nosazeogie_GBBG_movement_L2_highresonly_for_dryad.csv"))

##RW: with raw and CI

####loop

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# Create output directory if it doesn't exist
output_dir <- here(
  "data", "updated PlosOne figures" #plots
)

dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)


d6 <- d6 %>%
  mutate(date = as.POSIXct(date, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC"))



plot_data <- d6 %>%
    filter(id == 23335149) %>% # "211547A17"
    dplyr::select(date, id, z_raw, z_fit1, z_fit1.se) %>%
    mutate(
      lower = z_fit1 - (1.96*z_fit1.se),
      upper = z_fit1 + (1.96*z_fit1.se)
    )
  
  # Plot
p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = as.POSIXct(date))) +
    # Raw data as black points
    geom_point(aes(y = z_raw, group=1), color = "black", alpha = 0.6, size = 0.7) +
    # Confidence ribbon for RW
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "red", alpha = 0.3) +
    # RW as red line
    geom_line(aes(y = z_fit1), color = "red", size = 1) +
    
    labs(
      # title = paste("raw (points) vs RW (line)_highres_1sects", track_id),
      x = "Datetime", y = "Altitude (m)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()+
    theme(
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12,
      family = "serif", face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12,
      family = "serif", face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10,
      family = "serif"),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10,
      family = "serif")
    )

print(p)

# Save plot

ggsave(filename = file.path(output_dir, paste0("timeseries_23335149", ".tiff")),
         plot = p, width = 8, height = 3, dpi = 300)

```
